== Westergard identity and relationship check (2026-10-20) ==
* '''"Dan Westergard" is Jan.''' No SWCCG source names a Dan Westergard. The 2010 Worlds Day 2 decks once filed as "Dan Westergard" now redirect to Jan's deck pages. They match Jan: the Day 2 final standings posted by the Tournament Advocate list "15. Jan Westergard 10 +24" (forum topic t=37391, post p572198, 20 August 2010), and Jan also played the LOTR TCG Worlds held at the same event. The 2010 Day 2 p117/p118 scans were not used (Bill asked for them to be deleted).
* '''Family link: not sourced.''' The 2009 MPC pre-registration list (forum t=22347, 9 August 2008) has "Jan Westergard - MD Ghosttrain" next to "Chris Westergard - MD yodad". On 20 June 2022 yodad (Chris) posted in forum topic t=80947 (page 2, post p1380006) as a father whose sons played SWCCG, but the post does not name Jan. Nothing in print says Jan and Chris are married or related, so the article makes no claim. Nothing suggests a married couple.
* '''Ian Westergaard (2008).''' [[Jan Westergard|Ian Westergaard]] (2008 Worlds Day 2, DS p106, Team p27) sits in the same Day 2 PDF as Jan's 2008 lists (pp96–97). It is left as a separate page: the handwriting does not settle whether "Ian" is a misread of "Jan" or another player. The 2008 "Dan Westergaard" team reading is the same open question.
* '''2024 NAC and 2023 Worlds "Day 1" numbers.''' On the event pages the "Day 1" column is the row number of the alphabetical PC list, not a finish. Jan's 2024 NAC finish was corrected from 45 to 38 and Chris's to 27 from the PC standings. The event pages themselves still need the same fix.
* '''2023 Worlds stubs merged.''' [[Jan Westergard|Westergard J]] now redirects here (2023 Worlds Day 1, 56th, Endor Operations / The Force Is Strong In My Family).

== Ian Westergaard merged (2026-10-21) ==
[[Jan Westergard|Ian Westergaard]] is now a redirect here. This replaces the "Ian Westergaard (2008)" note above.
* Team sheet: page 27 of [[:File:2008 Worlds Team.pdf]] ([https://web.archive.org/web/20261008202922/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/tournaments/Decklists/2008/Worlds/2008+Worlds+Team.pdf Preserved copy]) has the handwritten player name "Jan Westergard". The deck is Light Side We'll Handle This.
* Day 2 sheet: page 96 of [[:File:2008 Worlds Day 2.pdf]] ([https://web.archive.org/web/20261008202350/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/tournaments/Decklists/2008/Worlds/2008+Worlds+D2.pdf Preserved copy]) reads "Jan Westergard", deck title "One-Trick Pony OR Qui-Gon Gin, Man of the Hour", We'll Handle This. The name is in the same hand as the Team sheet, and the two lists are near-identical Qui-Gon/podracing decks (Generator Core, Anakin's Pod, Boonta Eve Podrace, Boss Nass' Chambers, Wesa Gotta Grand Army, Booster In Pulsar Skate).
* The earlier note was wrong about page 106: that sheet is Tom Fredjord's. No 2008 sheet names an Ian. The hub's empty "Ian Westergaard" Day 2 row had no decks and no source of its own. The only Ian source was the Team sheet, where the capital J was read as an I. This is the same misreading as the 2009 "Ian W." above.
* No "Dan Westergaard" appears on the current [[2008 World Championship]] Team table. The pages next to p27 are Eier (p26) and Scott Lingrell (p28).
* Changes: the Team deck page was moved to [[2008 Worlds Team Jan Westergard LS We'll Handle This]] and the scan to [[:File:2008 Worlds Team p27 Jan Westergard LS.png]], with redirects left behind. The Team row and a misreading note were added here. The hub and [[People/W]] were updated. [[People]] still links [[Jan Westergard|Ian Westergaard]] (now a redirect), because that index fails the style lint on its existing paragraph lengths.
[[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 00:49, 21 October 2026 (UTC)
